name: Alcester 26/01376/FUL
md:
# 30 Hadrians Walk, Alcester

**[26/01376/FUL](https://apps.stratford.gov.uk/Eplanningv2/AppDetail/Index/17a0bc82-221b-c690-1c04-08debd514ecb)** · Stratford-on-Avon District Council · officer (delegated) · decided 17 September 2026 · **refused**

Erection of 2no dwellings and associated external works (resubmission of planning application No:25/02296/FUL).

[Planning record](https://apps.stratford.gov.uk/Eplanningv2/AppDetail/Index/17a0bc82-221b-c690-1c04-08debd514ecb)

**Cited in:** 1. DP3(3) as a "should be refused" policy

## Key points

- The site is partly in flood zones 2 and 3: "with the western part of the site falling into Flood Zones 2 and 3" (p.8). "NDMP F7 is explicit that development should be refused unless all of the requirements of NDMP F7 are addressed" (p.9).
- The officer applied S4(2)(c): "the proposal would fail against NDMP F7, and the proposal would fall into one of the specific reasons to refuse an application with the framework … Therefore the presumption in favour of development would not apply" (p.3). S4(2)(c) makes the benefits "likely to be substantially outweighed"; it does not switch the presumption off.
- The decision notice also records that insufficient information was provided on the habitat baseline of the site.

*Quotations are from the officer report, decision notice or appeal decision letter, with page (p.) or paragraph (¶) numbers. Read the decision itself for the full reasoning.*

name: Snitterfield 26/00617/PIP
md:
# Land off Jago Green, Snitterfield Lane, Snitterfield

**[26/00617/PIP](https://apps.stratford.gov.uk/Eplanningv2/AppDetail/Index/aa9dde59-9cff-c42a-4559-08de7ebaa5be)** · Stratford-on-Avon District Council · Planning Committee, 9 September 2026 · notice 10 September 2026 · **granted**

Permission in principle for a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 5 dwellings, including pedestrian access to Park Lane, on open countryside adjacent to the built-up area boundary. The village is washed over by the Green Belt; the report found the scheme not inappropriate under GB7.

[Planning record](https://apps.stratford.gov.uk/Eplanningv2/AppDetail/Index/aa9dde59-9cff-c42a-4559-08de7ebaa5be) · [Committee report](https://democracy.stratford.gov.uk/documents/s78474/26.00617.PIP%20-%20Jago%20Green%20FINAL.pdf) · [Minutes and Update Report](https://democracy.stratford.gov.uk/documents/g6929/Public%20minutes%2009th-Sep-2026%2018.00%20Planning%20Committee.pdf?T=11)

**Cited in:** 1. DP3(3) as a "should be refused" policy; 3. The reason given for discounting CS.8; 5. Walking routes and stations

## Key points

- Character: "I consider that the proposal would result in significant harm to the character of the area" (p.15); the scheme "would not accord with Policies CS.5, CS.9 and CS.12 of the Core Strategy and NDP Policies BE1, BE3 and NE4" (p.15); "In light of NDMP DP3 (3), I afford this harm substantial weight" (p.15).
- Route: the report applied "NDMP S5.1, Part J (Principle of development outside settlements)" (p.9) before turning to GB7.
- The report quotes S5(5) including "decision-making policies in this Framework, and applying paragraph 2 of this policy" (p.10), but its conclusion does not apply S5(2): "I conclude that the benefits of approving the scheme would not be substantially outweighed by any adverse effects" (p.20).
- CS.8: HE5 "provides a new set of criteria for assessments of the potential effects on development proposals on the significance of heritage assets which is not required within CS.8 of the CS and BE7 of the NDP, I consider that CS.8 and BE7 are materially inconsistent with the NDMPs of the Framework" (p.15). The report later finds "the development would accord with NDMPs HE5 and HE6 of the Framework and Policy CS.8 of the Core Strategy" (p.16).
- Walking route: the report accepted "some harm that pedestrians will have to walk on the public highway" (p.9). The Update Report for the 9 September committee corrected this, because "the application proposes a footpath onto Park Lane": "the centre of the village and services can be reached entirely on made footpath and do not require any pedestrians to walk in the public highway" (minutes and Update Report, p.5).

*Quotations are from the officer report, decision notice or appeal decision letter, with page (p.) or paragraph (¶) numbers. Read the decision itself for the full reasoning.*

name: Forest Farm, Long Marston 26/01906/PIP
md:
# Forest Farm, Welford Road, Long Marston

**[26/01906/PIP](https://apps.stratford.gov.uk/Eplanningv2/AppDetail/Index/57492042-a67c-c119-4332-08deef0d708e)** · Stratford-on-Avon District Council · officer (delegated) · decided 22 September 2026 · **granted**

Permission in principle for one residential dwelling beside the Grade II listed Forest Farmhouse and Lyndon Cottage.

[Planning record](https://apps.stratford.gov.uk/Eplanningv2/AppDetail/Index/57492042-a67c-c119-4332-08deef0d708e)

**Cited in:** 2. Heritage harm at Forest Farm; 3. The reason given for discounting CS.8

## Key points

- Harm: "the proposals will be highly detrimental to the dwelling's setting" (p.7); and "the design would be contrary to the statutory requirements of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) 1990 Act" (p.8).
- CS.8: HE5 "provides a new set of criteria for assessments of the potential effects on development proposals on the significance of heritage assets which is not required within CS.8, I consider that CS.8 is materially inconsistent with the NDMPs of the Framework" (p.6). The report then finds "The development would fail to accord with CS.8 of the Core Strategy" (p.8) and counts that conflict as harm.
- Conclusion: the harm "is afforded substantial adverse weight, this is in conflict with CS.8 of the Core Strategy and NDP Policy HA.1 and NDMP HE6" (p.10); one dwelling towards "the currently substandard housing land supply, which is afforded substantial positive weight" (p.10); and "the benefits of approving the scheme would not be substantially outweighed by any adverse effects" (p.10).
- The report does not weigh the harm against public benefits under HE6(4). Its only reference to public benefits is in its quotation of neighbourhood plan policy HA.1.

*Quotations are from the officer report, decision notice or appeal decision letter, with page (p.) or paragraph (¶) numbers. Read the decision itself for the full reasoning.*

# Land off Butts Lane, Tanworth-in-Arden

**[26/00918/PIP](https://apps.stratford.gov.uk/Eplanningv2/AppDetail/Index/ac388915-f51c-c846-534c-08de96df9034)** · Stratford-on-Avon District Council · Planning Committee, 9 September 2026 · notice 11 September 2026 · **granted**

Permission in principle for a minimum of three and a maximum of nine dwellings, in a village washed over by the Green Belt.

[Planning record](https://apps.stratford.gov.uk/Eplanningv2/AppDetail/Index/ac388915-f51c-c846-534c-08de96df9034) · [Committee report](https://democracy.stratford.gov.uk/documents/s78472/26.00918.PIP%20%20Butts%20Lane%20Tanworth%20cttee.pdf) · [Minutes and Update Report](https://democracy.stratford.gov.uk/documents/g6929/Public%20minutes%2009th-Sep-2026%2018.00%20Planning%20Committee.pdf?T=11)

**Cited in:** 4. Location shortcuts in the Green Belt; 5. Walking routes and stations

## Key points

- S5(1)(j) test applied: the report named "NDMP S5.1, Part J (Principle of development outside settlements)" (p.8) and found "the development would be well-related to an existing settlement and would be of a scale that the local settlement could accommodate" (p.9).
- Walking route, in the S5 and TR3 section: "some sections of that walk do not benefit from pavements" (p.9); "the absence of pavements is for very short lengths only and on not especially busy roads and where speeds are low" (p.9). "Villagers appear to cope with this existing situation without any great trouble" (p.9).
- The report then applied GB7, relying on that assessment for limb (iii): "As set out above, it is acknowledged that there are pavements linking the site to the rest of the village" (p.13). It added that Tanworth "Tanworth in Arden is a Local Service Village and as such is considered to be a sustainable settlement" (p.13), and passed limb (iii) "despite the identified conflicts with Policies CS.15, CS.16 and AS.10" (p.13).

*Quotations are from the officer report, decision notice or appeal decision letter, with page (p.) or paragraph (¶) numbers. Read the decision itself for the full reasoning.*

md:
# 126 Toms Lane, Kings Langley

**Appeal [6011803](https://appeal-planning-decision.service.gov.uk/comment-planning-appeal/appeals/6011803)** · Three Rivers District Council · Planning Inspector · decided 9 September 2026 · **dismissed**

Demolition of existing building and construction of replacement and infill dwellings, on a site washed over by the Green Belt.

[Case page](https://appeal-planning-decision.service.gov.uk/comment-planning-appeal/appeals/6011803) · [Decision letter](https://appeal-planning-decision.service.gov.uk/published-document/63c01be5-5483-47df-aba5-ec0f6a77ba73)

**Cited in:** 1. DP3(3) as a "should be refused" policy; 4. Location shortcuts in the Green Belt

## Key points

- Green Belt: "the parties are in agreement that the proposal is not inappropriate development" (¶4).
- Route: "Paragraph 5 of policy S5 of the Framework explains, in summary, that where development would not be inappropriate, proposals should be approved unless the benefits of doing so would be substantially outweighed" (¶17).
- The council argued S4 applied; the inspector noted "the site is designated in the Local Plan as being washed over by the Green Belt" (¶18), adding "Even if the area is viewed as a built-up area where policy S4 of the Framework would apply" (¶19), the concerns would remain.
- DP3(3): "the proposal would fail to comply with one of the national decision-making policies, namely paragraph 3 of policy DP3, where there is a clear conflict with policy DM1 of the TRLDD insofar as it relates to the development of backland homes" (¶20). "This policy of the Framework directs that the proposal should be refused" (¶20).

md:
# Land off Oakdene Crescent, Hatton, Warwick

**Appeal [6006637](https://appeal-planning-decision.service.gov.uk/comment-planning-appeal/appeals/6006637)** · Warwick District Council · Planning Inspector, after a hearing · decided 23 September 2026 · **dismissed**

Redevelopment of the site and erection of 28 residential dwellings, in the Green Belt, about 350 m from Hatton railway station.

[Case page](https://appeal-planning-decision.service.gov.uk/comment-planning-appeal/appeals/6006637) · [Decision letter](https://appeal-planning-decision.service.gov.uk/published-document/701d49de-a57d-40d1-ab37-2ad4d152121c)

## Key points

- Station: "the station does not meet the Framework's definition of a 'well-connected station'" (¶18).
- Route: "I also accept that the absence of continuous footways does not automatically render Station Road unsuitable for pedestrian use. Nonetheless … Station Road cannot reasonably be regarded as providing a safe route for all users, particularly pedestrians" (¶24).
- Observed use: "it is likely that at least some journeys arise out of necessity rather than choice. In such circumstances, the recorded levels of activity do not demonstrate that the route is universally perceived as safe" (¶26).

**Cited in:** 5. Walking routes and stations

## Key points

- Settlement: "The nearest settlement to the appeal site is Findon which is a service village" (¶15).
- Route: an unlit lane with no footway, so "I consider the appeal site not to be well connected to Findon, and future occupiers would have a reliance on the private car" (¶15).
- Conclusion: "future residents would likely be highly reliant on private cars for most journeys, irrespective of the precise distance. In this context the proposed development would not be physically well related to the settlement of Findon" (¶17).

**Cited in:** 5. Walking routes and stations

## Key points

- Settlement: Banks is "identified in the LP as a 'Key Sustainable Village.'" (¶9).
- Location: "the distance to the nearest services and facilities in Banks would mean that future occupiers of the proposed dwelling would be largely reliant on the private car to meet their day-to-day needs" (¶14).
- The conversion was not inappropriate in the Green Belt, so the poor location counted as harm in the S5(5) balance, and the appeal was allowed on that balance (¶29–32).
